clue.text: Fifty hosted by wonderful boy, full house on the cards?

parts.note: grand means splendid or wonderful

indicators.note: the fifty is a guest held within the boy's name

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A card player hits a winning streak, with fifty points and a full house in the offing.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the slam where a side wins all thirteen tricks is the biggest; 'full house' here means every trick taken, not the poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning every trick in bridge is called this contract, a clean sweep of the cards, hence a full house of tricks.

clue.text: Some sheep had been procured by Joe?

parts.note: GI Joe is the nickname for an American soldier, so Joe gives GI
got means obtained or procured

explanation.surface: A farmer asks whether Joe acquired a few of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some sheep' means part of a sheep, not a number of animals: the answer is a cut of meat. Joe is the American soldier, GI Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: This French term names a leg of lamb or mutton, which is a portion of a sheep.

clue.text: Outlaw putting car in reverse to access a part of motorway

indicators.note: the car gets into the lane, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a lane is one strip of a motorway's carriageway

indicators.note: the car's name is to be read backwards

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car

explanation.surface: A highwayman backs his car onto a slip road to reach the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lada is a Russian car. 'Outlaw' is the whole definition, a member of Robin Hood's band, spelt with hyphens.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the minstrel among Robin Hood's merry men, a band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: As a system of counting, doctor aided locum

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A stand-in GP was helped by a doctor, apparently in some counting scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun beside the locum, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange AIDED LOCUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting in base twelve, with dozens as the unit, is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: See 18
Island prowler, Mo?

definitions.meaning: a tailless breed of cat from an island in the Irish Sea
Mo is the word mog, slang for a cat, with its tail missing: a tailless cat

explanation.surface: Someone named Mo is suspected of prowling round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: MOG is British slang for a cat; cut off its last letter and you have a tailless cat in miniature. The Isle of Man is in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed from the Isle of Man is famous for having no tail, matching a docked mog.

clue.text: Pirate school

definitions.meaning: Edward ..., better known as Blackbeard, was a notorious pirate
as a verb, to school someone is to instruct them

explanation.surface: A buccaneer academy, as a two-word picture.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is Blackbeard's real surname; the other is a verb meaning to instruct or train.

clue.text: Covering for wheels, wheels in delivery truck

indicators.note: wheels says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that covers the wheels of a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unused; it is the hiding signal. The second 'wheels' is a verb, to turn round, so the letters ERYT found in 'delivery truck' are turned to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber casing fitted round the rim covers each road wheel of a vehicle.

clue.text: A topmost chamber starts to describe it, looking up?

definitions.text: A topmost chamber starts to describe it, looking up?

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the initials enclose the next piece
the starts of the first three words supply their initial letters
in a down entry, looking up means reading the word upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks how to describe the highest room in a house, with one's eyes turned upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' wraps ATC (the starts of A Topmost Chamber) round TI, which is 'it' looking up.
explanation.definitionFit: The room just under the roof is the highest chamber in a house, the one you look up to.

clue.text: House here's so dilapidated — is that lucky?

definitions.note: the definition asks about a thing: a common good-luck charm

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so the letters of these words are in ruins

explanation.surface: A buyer viewing a ruined house wonders if their luck is in.
explanation.walkthrough: HO stays as it is; only 'here's so' is rearranged, by 'dilapidated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved iron shoe nailed above a door is a traditional charm for good fortune.

clue.text: Waste killer having stolen a ring

indicators.note: the weapon takes the letter into itself

parts.note: a gun is a lethal weapon, a killer
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wasteful murderer grabs a ring as loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Seabird and bat droppings, collected as fertiliser, are animal waste.

clue.text: Back of mining engineer nearer to dynamo

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mining engineer edges closer to the dynamo at the back of the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' is a verb here, not the person by the dynamo.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine that produces electricity, one type of electricity producer.

clue.text: What might clamp puzzle in China?

parts.note: a teaser is a brain-teaser, a puzzle
a vice is a bench tool that clamps work

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking what might hold a riddle tight inside China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' at the start of a sentence hides that it means crockery, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of porcelain cups, saucers and teapot is fine china.

clue.text: See 20
Refrain from cutting half-baked loaves somewhere in Eastern Europe

indicators.note: the stopping word cuts into the scrambled loaves
half-baked means badly thought out, so the loaves come out misshapen

parts.note: to stop doing something is to refrain from it

explanation.surface: A baker in Eastern Europe should stop cutting badly made bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts STOP inside SEVAOL, the loaves rearranged by 'half-baked'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an older spelling of the Crimean port of Sevastopol, a city on the Black Sea.

clue.text: A king boarding plane that's less reliable

indicators.note: the passengers board the plane, getting inside it

parts.note: a flier is an aircraft
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch climbs aboard an aircraft that is not very dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaky means unreliable, so the comparative describes someone even less dependable.

clue.text: Angle bottle round food

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
bottle and balls are both British slang for courage

explanation.surface: An angler wraps a bottle round some food.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls of minced fish, fried or poached, are small round dishes.

clue.text: Ordinal left with less information originally, after amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters text, so the remaining letters are rearranged
less means without, taking a letter away
originally points to the first letter of information

explanation.surface: A list of ordinal numbers is left with less information after being edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes I (the first letter of information, from 'originally') from LEFT WITH, and 'after amendment' rearranges LEFTWTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal number gives a position in a sequence; this one comes after eleventh.

clue.text: Suspicion initially in patient poking not entirely cooked dish

indicators.note: the patient pokes into the shortened cooking word
the cooking word loses its final letter

parts.note: fried means cooked in fat

indicators.note: the letter goes within the patient

parts.note: a case is a patient under a doctor's care

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Suspicion

explanation.surface: A suspicious patient pokes at a dish that is undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely cooked' looks like the definition of something raw, but it is wordplay; only 'dish' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew of meat in a white sauce is a classic French dish.

clue.text: As was the queen of biblical kingdom — good for an affair

parts.words: As was the queen of biblical kingdom
parts.note: the Queen of Sheba was a native of that kingdom, a Sheban

explanation.surface: The Queen of Sheba, a good match for a royal affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheban is the adjective for Sheba, the biblical kingdom whose queen visited Solomon.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'the whole shebang', the word means an affair, a business or matter.

clue.text: Produce the toys for building minister up, mate!

parts.note: to get is to obtain or produce
one's stands for the possessive the, as in 'get one's coat'
Lego is a construction toy of interlocking bricks

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A vicar is told to take out the building bricks: 'Pass them up, mate!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' looks like the friendly address at the end of a sentence; it is a verb, the definition. The phrase is crude British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: This is crude British slang for having sex, and 'mate' as a verb means to couple.

clue.text: Dine out on candy? A potential killer!

parts.note: read candy as C and Y, the two letters

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone warns that eating sweets could be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'candy' is to be read as 'C and Y', two letters; 'on' places the rearranged dine after them.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound is a fast-acting poison, so it can kill.

clue.text: Short swirl in cleaner dairy produce

indicators.note: the cut swirl sits inside the cleaner

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl in water

explanation.surface: A brief swirl of the mop by a cleaner in the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' is British for a domestic cleaner, a charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheese from the Somerset village is a dairy product.

clue.text: Niap?

parts.note: the word pain written backwards

explanation.surface: A nonsense word with a question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: ACHE (a pain) with BACK, so pain reversed gives NIAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the lower spine is the familiar complaint, and the clue's pain is itself turned round.

clue.text: Flasher and streaker, bottom covered in wake?

indicators.note: the bottom letter, in a down entry, is hidden away

parts.note: to come to is to wake up

explanation.surface: An exhibitionist streaks with their bottom covered, and someone wakes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom covered' hides the last letter of COME TO. Flasher and streaker suggest exhibitionists, not a celestial body flashing across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright body with a tail flashes and streaks across the night sky.

clue.text: Letters sent abroad by a politician, way lighter

indicators.note: letters sent abroad are scattered far and wide, so rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician sends letters overseas, which are much lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way lighter' looks like 'much less heavy', but is a light for a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a way, and a lamp on a post lights it.

clue.text: Constant love: our lot devoted to God

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
our lot means us

explanation.surface: A believer speaks of constant love from our community devoted to God.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious people are devout, earnestly devoted to God.

clue.text: See 26
Figure going into school after strike taken off

indicators.note: the school with its figure comes after the strike

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike

indicators.note: the number goes inside the school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A striking teacher has walked out, with a figure going into school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' means imitated in mockery, not removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them mockingly, which is ridicule in satire.

clue.text: Is island in rush for cocktail?

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the rush

parts.note: to pour is to rush out in a stream
taken as written
Kos, also spelt Cos, is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A traveller on an island asks whether to rush for a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink of Peruvian brandy with lime and egg white is a popular South American cocktail.

clue.text: Iodine in lead instrument

indicators.note: the element sits within the lead

parts.note: the lead in a film is its star
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Iodine inside lead, like a chemistry experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' wants to be the metal, but it is the leading actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked Indian lute is a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Small tots, primarily on wheels — in these?

definitions.text: Small tots, primarily on wheels — in these?

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letters of the two words

parts.note: rollers are small wheels

explanation.surface: Little children are pushed around on wheels, in these.
explanation.walkthrough: The American name for a pushchair; 'primarily' takes the starts of Small and tots.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children ride in wheeled pushchairs, which Americans call by this name.
